clue.text: Measure old court, when leaving

indicators.note: leaving says the word for when departs from the old court's name

parts.note: the assizes were the periodic county courts of England and Wales, abolished in 1971
as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: A legal historian takes the measure of a former court at the point it closed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes AS from ASSIZE; the trimmed court name gives the measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the measure of a garment or object is its dimensions or magnitude.

clue.text: Astronomer is firm: 'Highly injurious to ignore moon'

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: to ignore the moon means leaving it out of the word for highly injurious

parts.note: pernicious means highly injurious or destructive
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: An astronomer declares firmly that pretending the moon is not there would be very harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore' is the deletion signal; the moon is Jupiter's, not ours, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Polish astronomer who placed the sun, not the earth, at the centre of the solar system.

clue.text: A mistake, to include Irish browser

indicators.note: to include means the mistake word takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a gaffe is a blunder or mistake

explanation.surface: Someone surfing the web makes an error that involves something Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'browser' reads as web software, but here it is an animal that browses, feeding on leaves high in trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that feed on shoots and leaves are browsers, and this long-necked African animal is the classic example.

clue.text: Take horse on a public way, in this position?

indicators.note: on means the riding comes after the street in the down-the-line order of letters

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a public way
to take horse is the old phrase for to ride

explanation.surface: A rider takes to the street on horseback, sitting in exactly that posture.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: riding a horse along a street, you sit with legs on either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with one leg on each side of a horse is the posture of a rider, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Amusing story about odd team having a row?

definitions.text: Amusing story about odd team having a row?

parts.words: Amusing story about odd team having a row?
parts.note: Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel follows three friends rowing up the Thames; the odd team is the trio, and the row is a trip with oars, not a quarrel

explanation.surface: A funny tale about a mismatched group falling out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it means rowing a boat: the 1889 comic novel is about three friends rowing up the River Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel of a Thames boating holiday, an amusing story about a trio rowing.

clue.text: Cut short, perhaps, a specific point

definitions.meaning: to remove a tail, as when docking an animal, cutting it short
a single particular item or point

explanation.surface: Something trimmed back might still make one particular point.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a particular item or fact, and, split as de-tail, to remove a tail and so cut something short.

clue.text: Don't omit some eye movement, a bit glowing

parts.note: REM is rapid eye movement, the phase of sleep with dreaming
an ember is a small glowing piece of coal or wood

explanation.surface: A reminder not to forget some movement of the eyes and a faintly glowing fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of forgetting or leaving out: to keep something in mind is not to omit it.

clue.text: Sea creature has cold rear, swimming

indicators.note: swimming suggests letters moving about freely, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sea creature has a chilly rear end as it swims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges COLD and REAR into the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the precious coral of the Mediterranean, a marine animal colony valued for jewellery.

clue.text: Cost of running to the top of the tower

parts.note: up means to the top, as in climbing up
a keep is the strong central tower of a castle

explanation.surface: A climb to the top of a castle tower is what running it costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' means running a property, not jogging, and 'of the' only links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost of maintenance, what it takes to keep a house or car running.

clue.text: Don't tell people exciting women need beauty

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Keep this quiet: thrilling women require good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom said before a confidence: the speaker asks that the secret stay private and not be passed on to others.

clue.text: Channel extremely briefly captured by religious group

indicators.note: captured by means the shortened word is held inside the group

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect

indicators.note: briefly asks for the word to be cut short by its final letter

parts.note: very means extremely

explanation.surface: A religious sect very briefly seizes a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely briefly' looks like one phrase meaning 'very quickly', but 'briefly' is the curtailment signal acting on the word for 'extremely', and 'captured by' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A culvert is a tunnel or drain carrying water under a road, a kind of channel.

clue.text: Top, but try to avoid one school subject (English)

indicators.note: to avoid says the word try is left out of the subject's name

parts.note: chemistry is a subject taught at school

explanation.surface: A pupil tops the class but tries to dodge one subject, English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a garment, not first place; 'to avoid' takes TRY out of CHEMISTRY, leaving CHEMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemise is a loose shirt-like garment for women, worn on the upper body: a top.

clue.text: Ballet enthusiast takes the biscuit

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut
a cracker is a thin crisp biscuit

explanation.surface: A ballet fan's behaviour is the limit, it really takes the biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the biscuit', a British idiom for being outrageous, only hides the charade link 'takes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's Christmas ballet, an example of the ballet repertoire.

clue.text: A lot of animals tried to speak

indicators.note: to speak means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: heard as a judge hears a case, i.e. tried it

explanation.surface: Many animals attempted to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tried' is a court sense: a judge hears and tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a large group of cattle or other animals kept or living together.

clue.text: Noticed as having sense

definitions.meaning: able to see, having the sense of sight

explanation.surface: Someone sensible was spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: spotted or seen at a distance, and possessing vision rather than being blind.

clue.text: Not taxed, wound up speech welcoming a new leader

indicators.note: welcoming a new leader means the first letter is replaced by another

parts.note: to perorate is to sum up a speech, so perorated means concluded a speech

explanation.surface: An untaxed speaker ended their address by greeting a newly chosen leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming a new leader' swaps the P at the head of PERORATED for a different letter, Z.
explanation.definitionFit: In UK VAT, zero-rated goods are taxable at a rate of nothing, so in effect no tax is charged.

clue.text: Key batsman

definitions.meaning: a tin or bottle ... does the job of a key, opening things
an opening batsman in cricket goes in first

explanation.surface: An important cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the two batsmen who start an innings are its openers.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a tool or key that opens something, and a cricketer who begins the batting.

clue.text: One free of underground work accepts a schoolmasterly role

indicators.note: accepts means the former miner takes the article inside

parts.note: an ex-miner no longer works underground

explanation.surface: A retired miner takes up a teaching job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' places A inside EX-MINER.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting and marking tests is a schoolmaster's task, so an examiner plays a schoolmasterly role.

clue.text: Be hopeless, as ministers unprepared for service?

definitions.meaning: to have no chance at all of success
clergy who arrive at a church service with no prayer ready, taking the idiom literally

explanation.surface: Vicars without a prayer ready for the service are doomed.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for having no chance at all, read literally as clergy lacking a prayer for worship.

clue.text: One leg lifted, beneath check material …

indicators.note: beneath means these letters come below the check abbreviation in the down entry

parts.note: ch is the chess abbreviation for check
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A leg is raised under checked fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side; 'lifted' turns ON to NO in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a twilled cotton cloth used for trousers, so a material.

clue.text: … is one too hot wearing this?

definitions.text: … is one too hot wearing this?

parts.words: … is one too hot wearing this?
parts.note: a woollen jumper makes the wearer perspire when it is too warm, so the garment is named after the effect

explanation.surface: Continuing the material clue: is someone overheated in this garment?
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 7 down's material; a jumper is called this because it may make the wearer perspire.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted pullover, which a person overheating in it would literally make sweat.

clue.text: Snub one that has jumped into the canal?

definitions.text: one that has jumped into the canal?
definitions.meaning: a jumping insect that has leapt into the ear canal, taking the idiom literally

explanation.surface: Someone who leapt into a waterway is cold-shouldered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canal' looks like a waterway but is the ear canal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a sharp rebuff, read literally as a jumping insect lodged in the ear canal.

clue.text: Diner able to change waiters for free food

definitions.note: a plural phrase for a queue of people waiting; the answer names that queue

indicators.note: to change means the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer is able to swap waiting staff in exchange for a free meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waiters' are not restaurant staff but people waiting, in a queue for food handouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadline is a queue of poor people waiting for free food, so the waiters themselves in line.

clue.text: Sort of attraction to capture in wizard work

indicators.note: in means the capture word goes inside the wizard's work

parts.note: magic is what a wizard does
to net is to catch or capture

explanation.surface: A wizard's spell works to capture a kind of attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic attraction is a physical force, and the adjective names that kind of pull.

clue.text: Clean holy image in fateful stream

parts.note: to rub something can clean it
an icon is a holy image in Orthodox Christianity

explanation.surface: Someone polishes a sacred picture beside a fateful river.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar's crossing of this small river in 49 BC began civil war, hence 'fateful'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rubicon is the Italian river Caesar crossed; crossing it means a point of no return.

clue.text: Ahead of time, submit church stipend

parts.note: pre- means before or ahead of time
to bend is to submit or yield

explanation.surface: A cleric gives in early over his church allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: A prebend is the allowance paid to a canon of a cathedral, a church stipend.

clue.text: I've been hit a lot, not the head — in part of foot

indicators.note: in means the shortened word sits inside the foot part

parts.note: a toe is part of a foot

indicators.note: not the head means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: much means a lot

explanation.surface: Someone struck many times, though not on the head, but in the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I've been hit' is a fencer's admission; 'not the head' drops a first letter, and 'in' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The fencer's call admitting a hit, borrowed from French; also used to concede a good point in argument.

clue.text: Make to leave Spanish city with time available

indicators.note: to leave means the word for make departs from the city's name

parts.note: Toledo is a city in central Spain
to do is to make, as in do a meal

explanation.surface: Instructions for leaving a Spanish city when there is time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make to leave' reads as an order to depart, but 'Make' is the word removed and 'to leave' the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign on a property for rent: it is available to be rented.
